title: Introduce cross-stage signal fabric and token attribution proxy
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Long-tail investigations showed that per-stage signal loss (drops between frontend, router, and serving stages) obscures token-level cost attribution and makes SLO blame messy. This PR introduces a light-weight cross-stage 'signal fabric' that tags and forwards minimal attribution tokens and introduces a proxy component that synthesizes a per-invocation token attribution trace. Goals: 1) make token-cost/latency attribution resilient to partial telemetry loss; 2) provide a compact join key for cross-stage tracing without increasing high-cardinality payloads; 3) enable a new dashboard for per-route token-attribution heatmaps and an alert that suppresses noise when attribution confidence is low. Design summary: - Signal fabric: small in-process publisher/subscriber with protobuf-encoded envelopes; each envelope carries a compact attribution header (trace_id, invocation_id, token_hashes[], stage_vector) and optional sampling hints. The fabric is pluggable: implemented in observability/collector as SignalFabric interface with in-memory and grpc-forwarder implementations. - Token attribution proxy: a lightweight aggregator (observability/attributor) that listens to fabric events and joins partial signals using a time-bucketed bloom join; it outputs a canonical attribution record per invocation. The join strategy favors recall for debugging (configurable to favor precision for billing pipelines). - Backward compatibility: components fall back to existing behavior if the fabric is disabled. The fabric attaches a small header to existing spans (no change to RPC payloads). Implementation notes: - New packages: observability/fabric (fabric API + inproc impl), observability/attributor (joiner + exporter), telemetry/protos/attribution.proto (message definitions) - Hooked fabric into route-router (router/ingest.go) and serving runtime pre-KV-flush path; the router publishes prefix-warmup and multi-stage scheduling hints while runtime publishes token-phase markers. - Efficiency: payloads are compact (<256B typical). Fabric uses scatter-gather with bounded queues and cooperative backpressure so critical fast-paths never block. - Configuration: default ON for dedicated/private deploys, OFF for hosted by default; rollout gated by feature flag redwood.observability.crossstage_fabric. Tests & CI: - Unit tests for bloom joiner, envelope roundtrip, and backpressure paths added. - Integration test harness in ci/observability-integration.yml spins up inproc fabric + attributor and validates end-to-end attribution for synthetic traces (coldstart, burst, partial-loss). - One flaky integration test (joiner/flaky-window) initially failed due to timer skew; fixed by tighter clock drift tolerance and re-run in CI. Files changed (high-level): observability/fabric/fabric.go, observability/fabric/inproc.go, observability/attributor/attributor.go, telemetry/protos/attribution.proto, dashboards/token-attribution-dashboard.json, docs/observability/signal-fabric.md, ci/observability-integration.yml Migration plan: - Canary rollout: enable flag for 5% of traffic in us-west-2, monitor attribution coverage and CPU on the attributor service. - Observability: new dashboards added (token attribution coverage, join latency, attribution confidence histogram) and an alert (ATB-01) that triggers if attribution coverage drops >10% or join-latency 95p > 2s. - Rollback: disable feature flag and drain attributor queues; the system will revert to per-stage raw spans. Security & privacy: we avoid storing token plaintexts — the fabric only exchanges token_hashes and size-limited context blobs. Operational notes: this introduces a new service job (attributor) that should be co-located in the observability tier; resource estimates: ~0.5 vCPU per 1000 rps of observed invocations, memory modest (128MB per shard) Remaining work (follow-ups): - Add an opt-in precision mode for billing pipelines that retains exact token indices (requires vault KMS review) - Dashboard drilldown widgets for invocation-level reconstructed traces - Add a Prometheus exporter for attributor internals Rollout/merge notes: landed after approvals and CI re-run. All changes behind feature flag to avoid customer impact.

1) init: add attribution proto and fabric interface

review_comments: Leo Ramirez: Could the bloom-joiner produce false positives that bias cost allocation? Please add a confidence score per record.
Aisha Patel (author): Added per-record attribution_confidence (0-100) exported to the dashboard; default joiner params tuned for low FP.
Daniel Kim: Small nit - inproc queues should expose a metrics tag for queue_depth by shard. Also, please mark the attributor pod as BestEffort in the chart?
Aisha Patel (author): Added queue_depth metric and updated helm chart suggestion (docs/observability/signal-fabric.md) with resource guidance; left scheduling as Burstable for now per perf team ask.
Soren Dahl: Integration test failed on first run (joiner window). After the skew fix I re-ran and tests passed. Please note in the changelog why the timer tolerance increased.
ci_summary: Initial CI run: unit tests passed; integration job failed (joiner window flake). Fixed clock tolerance and pushed commit 5; re-ran CI. Final CI: all checks passed. Observability e2e test runtime ~4m. Coverage: +3.2% on observability package.
release_notes: Add cross-stage signal fabric and token attribution proxy: improves resilience for token-level cost and latency attribution across multi-stage request paths. Adds dashboards and an alert for attribution coverage. Default off for hosted; feature-flagged rollout for dedicated/private.
notes_for_oncall: If ATB-01 fires (attribution coverage drop or join-latency spike), first check attributor pod logs for 'join-window-exceeded' errors, verify feature flag rollout percentage, and if needed disable redwood.observability.crossstage_fabric for the affected region to restore prior behavior.
